milestones.name: Sign both sides in and read the record behind each name
Submit an invoice, see what it costs, and have it tokenized
Fund the invoice: Privy approves the money, Hedera moves the asset
Sell half to a second investor on day 20
Repay on day 60 and pay every holder its share
Let that outcome price the business's next invoice

goals.statement: Sign both sides in and read the record behind each name
Submit an invoice, see what it costs, and have it tokenized
Fund the invoice: Privy approves the money, Hedera moves the asset
Sell half to a second investor on day 20
Repay on day 60 and pay every holder its share
Let that outcome price the business's next invoice

steps.trigger: a freight company wants to finance an invoice and holds no key
steps.action: The judge signs in to the business portal with their own email and the six-digit code Privy sends it, and is seated as Ironline Freight's third director
steps.outcome: they can now approve what the company wallet does — one of the two signatures it takes — which is what makes this a demo anyone can run rather than watch

steps.trigger: the portal names the company instead of showing a wallet address
steps.action: Clicking the name opens ironline.business.receivablesflow.eth/records — six invoices financed here and all six settled: 4 paid on time, 2 late, none defaulted
steps.outcome: the history everything after this is priced from is public, and nobody had to ask us for it

steps.trigger: a fund wants short, secured returns and holds no key either
steps.action: The same judge signs in to the investor portal in the next tab, as Woodgrove Capital
steps.outcome: no seat is needed on this side: the fund's wallet is governed by a mandate rather than by signatures, so it refuses what breaks the rules no matter who is signed in

steps.trigger: the fund is named on its own screen the same way
steps.action: Clicking it opens woodgrove.investor.receivablesflow.eth/records — the standing that decides whether it may hold a receivable
steps.outcome: both sides are public names with public records before a single dollar moves

steps.trigger: the invoice is sent and Northwind has 60 days to pay it
steps.action: Ironline submits INV-2026-0417.pdf for financing — $50,000 from Northwind Supplies, payable 4 November
steps.outcome: the request is the document itself, openable from the portal

steps.trigger: the platform has to answer what that invoice is worth today
steps.action: It is priced off Ironline’s ENS record on the spot: 83 of 100 pays 0.067% a day — 4.02% over 60 days, so 60 days costs $2,010 and Ironline would receive $47,990
steps.outcome: the business sees the cost of the money before it commits to anything

steps.trigger: the company wallet takes two signatures of the three seats on it
steps.action: Ironline's own finance system signs the financing — one signature of the two, and never enough on its own
steps.outcome: what the wallet is still waiting for is a person

steps.trigger: the judge holds the third seat on that wallet
steps.action: They press Approve, their browser signs, and the two signatures go to Privy together — which counts them and sends the transaction
steps.outcome: nothing we wrote decided the sale was allowed; sending one signature is refused by the same button

steps.action: The invoice becomes RCV-0001 on Hedera — a token only investors the platform has KYC-approved can hold
steps.outcome: the claim now exists apart from Ironline, and whoever holds it on 4 November is owed the $50,000

steps.trigger: the fund is asked to put $47,990 into this invoice
steps.action: Privy checks it against the mandate written on the fund's wallet — under the $100,000 cap, above the 60 of 100 floor, on the rated list — and signs
steps.outcome: nothing in our code decides this; a breach is refused by the wallet itself, and the reason on screen is Privy’s own words

steps.trigger: the payment is authorised and the invoice has to change hands
steps.action: On Hedera, the settlement contract moves both sides at once — $47,990 to Ironline, RCV-0001 to Woodgrove — or neither moves
steps.outcome: nobody is paid without delivering, and nobody delivers without being paid

steps.trigger: the sale is done and repayment is sixty days away
steps.action: The repayment is scheduled on Hedera at the moment of sale, timed for day 60
steps.outcome: maturity runs on its own, with nobody to remind and nothing to chase

steps.trigger: on day 20 Woodgrove wants some of its money back without waiting for day 60
steps.action: Woodgrove sells half the invoice to Bridgeline Partners, another approved investor, and keeps the other half
steps.outcome: two investors now hold half each, and the invoice itself says so

steps.trigger: the half being sold has to have a price
steps.action: Same score, same rate — only 40 days are left instead of 60, so Bridgeline pays $24,025 for $25,000 due on day 60
steps.outcome: Woodgrove has $24,025 back on day 20 and still holds $25,000 of face value

steps.trigger: day 60 arrives and the customer has paid
steps.action: Northwind pays the invoice, Ironline repays the $50,000, and each holder is paid its half with its own transaction
steps.outcome: the split follows whoever the invoice says holds it, and nobody has to claim anything

steps.trigger: the day-60 outcome is settled either way
steps.action: The outcome is written back to Ironline’s ENS records — paid on time goes from 4 to 5, and the score from 83 to 86 — so its next invoice is quoted at a smaller discount; not paying does the reverse
steps.outcome: this invoice set the price of the next one, and the cycle starts again
